newsitem.title: USA: Snyder still mulling Patina options.
newsitem.headline: Snyder still mulling Patina options.

text.p: Snyder Oil Corp (SOCO) is still undecided as to whether it will selloff or complete a full acquisition of 74 percent-owned subsidiary Patina Oil & Gas Corp, former Snyder president Thomas Edelman told a conference call on Monday.

"We indicated from when before the deal was completed we expected sooner or later to come in fully to SOCO, or far more likely at least in my expectation, to go out as a separate entity to the benefit of SOCO," said Edelman, who resigned as president on Friday.
Edelman, who remains chairman and CEO of Patina, said that Patina could me demerged from Snyder either through a merger or the sale of stock.
However, Snyder chairman, John Snyder said that the issue was not clear yet and that rolling Patina into Snyder was not a poor alternative and may reduce some duplicate costs.
"The alternative we take may be opportunity driven," he said.

Edelman added that last year's sale of a 32.6 percent stake in Australia's Command Petroleum Holdings to Britain's Cairn Energy Plc had added substantially to Snyder's worth as Cairn itself is the subject of a hostile bid from Gulf Canada Resources Ltd.
"We now hold $5.00 per SOCO share in Cairn stock," Edelman said.
Snyder will release 1996 earnings on Thursday.
Snyder is also looking at selling off other international assets via an offering on the London Stock Exchange under the name of SOCO International.

"We are proceeding apace with an offering of our other international assets in the UK. We expect that offering to take place in May and if that proceeds on the basis we are expecting that will also generate a gain of several dollars per SOCO share," Edelman said.
